name: Martha K. Mwansa
currentRole: Senior Associate, AMW & Co. Legal Practitioners
bio: Martha Kaluba-Mwansa holds a place in the Guild's history as its founding President, establishing the foundation on which the Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia and its student executives have since built. She completed her Bachelor of Laws at the University of Zambia School of Law, where she was active in campus leadership. She is now an Advocate of the High Court and Supreme Court for Zambia and a Senior Associate at AMW & Co. Legal Practitioners in Lusaka. Her practice covers civil and commercial litigation, employment and labour law, and conveyancing. She is also an Associate of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (MCIArb). Outside her professional practice, she has volunteered as a legal assistant with UpZambia (the Undikumbukiri Project), an organisation that protects the rights of juveniles in the justice system.
achievements: First President, Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia
Advocate of the High Court and Supreme Court for Zambia
Associate, Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (MCIArb)
Pro bono legal assistant, UpZambia (Undikumbukiri Project)

name: Lumbanya Mulenga
bio: Lumbanya Judah Mulenga was the second President of the Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia, succeeding the founding President, Martha Kaluba-Mwansa. He earned his Bachelor of Laws with Merit from the University of Lusaka, where he received an award for his contributions to the School of Law. He remains involved with the Guild and was a panellist at its 2026 Annual General Meeting, speaking on SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). After passing the Legal Practitioners Qualifying Examinations through ZIALE, he was admitted to the Bar in December 2024 and is an Advocate of the High Court for Zambia. He practises as an Associate at Elias Chipimo & Partners, focusing on corporate and business advisory, commercial litigation, competition law and ESG governance. In 2026 he was appointed Secretary of the Law Association of Zambia's Dispute Resolution and Commercial Practice Committee. He is also committed to legal education. He co-founded the LMV Academy and has spent more than five years tutoring and mentoring undergraduate law students and aspiring advocates preparing for their examinations.
achievements: Second President, Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia
LLB with Merit, University of Lusaka, and School of Law contribution award
Advocate of the High Court for Zambia (admitted December 2024)
Secretary, LAZ Dispute Resolution and Commercial Practice Committee (2026)
Co-founder, LMV Academy

name: Rafeka Malunga
bio: Rapheka Malunga was the third President of the Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia, succeeding Lumbanya Mulenga. He completed his Bachelor of Laws at Cavendish University Zambia in 2023 and has since pursued postgraduate studies in human rights at the University of Zambia. He returned to the Guild as a panellist at its Annual General Meeting at Cavendish University, leading discussion on SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). A human rights advocate and governance and development specialist, he is active in youth networks and serves as a global YMCA ChangeAgent. His access-to-justice experience includes volunteering as a student intern with the Undikumbukire Project Zambia (UpZambia), which works to secure legal protection for children in conflict with the law, and serving as an administrator of the Jessup Moot Court competition in Zambia. In his community work, he pioneered the Tonse Tibelenge project under the Proactive Youths for Positive Change Initiative, which sponsors and supports vulnerable children in the shanty districts of Lusaka.
achievements: Third President, Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia
LLB, Cavendish University Zambia (2023)
Postgraduate studies in human rights, University of Zambia
Global YMCA ChangeAgent
Administrator, Jessup Moot Court Zambia
Founder, Tonse Tibelenge project

name: Mulubwa Chilando
bio: Mulubwa Chilando served as President of the Students' Law Association of Zambia (SLAZ), the organisation that laid the groundwork for what is now the Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia. He also chaired the University of Lusaka Law Association and graduated from the University of Lusaka with a Bachelor of Laws with Credit in October 2026, adding certificates in Media and Entertainment Law and in Business and the Law.
At continental level, he has served the African Law Students' Association (ALSA) as Regional Director and later as Special Advisor to the President on Foreign Policy.

He is an alumnus of the DLA Piper Global Scholarship (Cohort 6) and has completed a leadership certificate through the Saïd Business School at the University of Oxford. His practical experience includes internships with DLA Piper UK LLP in Munich, Simeza Sangwa & Associates, Chipoma Chilambwe Legal Practitioners and the National Legal Aid Board headquarters. He also tutors law at Luminary Innovision Academy and is the author of Chilando's Financial Accounting Booklet.
achievements: President, Students' Law Association of Zambia (SLAZ)
Regional Director and Special Advisor to the President on Foreign Policy, ALSA
Chairperson, University of Lusaka Law Association
LLB with Credit, University of Lusaka (October 2026)
DLA Piper Global Scholarship Alumnus (Cohort 6)

name: Mofya Bangwe
currentRole: Legal Officer, NFC Africa Mining Plc; Co-Founding Partner, M.I Resources and Capital Partners
bio: Mofya Kunda Bangwe held national office as President of the Students' Law Association of Zambia (SLAZ), the student body that preceded the Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia. At university level, he chaired the University of Lusaka Law Association. He has also served the Federation of African Law Students in a disciplinary role and is a member of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (CIArb) Young Members Group in Zambia.

His professional focus is mining and investment law. He is a Legal Officer at NFC Africa Mining Plc on the Zambian Copperbelt, and Co-Founding Partner of M.I Resources and Capital Partners, an advisory firm operating from Kitwe and Lusaka. The firm's work covers mining licensing, regulatory compliance, joint venture structures and transaction support.

He has also worked with the Chinese Mining Enterprises Association in Zambia (CMEAZ) on initiatives documenting the economic impact, job creation and skills transfer from large-scale mining investment in Zambia, and has been involved in advocacy for youth participation in civic life and democracy.
achievements: President, Students' Law Association of Zambia (SLAZ)
Chairperson, University of Lusaka Law Association
Co-Founding Partner, M.I Resources and Capital Partners
Legal Officer, NFC Africa Mining Plc
Member, CIArb Young Members Group Zambia

name: Simon C. Mwewa
bio: Simon C. Mwewa is the sixth National President of the Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia. He is a final-year law student at Lusaka Goldsmiths University College, where he served as the first President of the faculty's Law Association and as President of the student union.

An advocate for youth participation in governance, he led the Legal Advocacy and Constitutional Reforms Insakas across the Copperbelt and Lusaka provinces, teaching young citizens about their constitutional rights. He also launched his faculty's first Public Lecture, on the Separation of Powers, bringing constitutional law scholars to address students.

In 2025 he was lead counsel for his university's team at the Law Association of Zambia's annual moot court session, where he received an award of recognition for his constitutional argument. In October 2026 he was a speaker at the Zambia Law Development Commission's Law Conference at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre, presenting on how young people can shape law reform and national development.
achievements: 6th National President, Legal Scholars' Guild of Zambia
First President, Law Association, Lusaka Goldsmiths University College
